context:
Goal: guards refuse only what can do harm, and records say what main does.
Problem (rule): record frozen-path-resolves-shell-vars says "A `cp` with a frozen source is refused (`MUTATING_COMMAND` over-refuses `cp` and `mv` on purpose)." Main already allows `cp <frozen hook> /tmp/x`, and a test pins that allow. So the sentence is false on main, and changing a recorded decision needs your word.
Based on (read): main's docs/decisions/frozen-path-resolves-shell-vars.md (the Rule 7 paragraph) and hooks/test_guard.py case "frozen: cp FROM a frozen hook to scratch is a read", which expects allow; triage read both at 03:58 CST.
Based on (ruling): the same record's owner line (owner, 2026-10-07) covers env-var values only, not cp.
Departs from: the record says a cp from a frozen source is refused — it would say a cp from a frozen source is a read, and a frozen target is refused.
Meanwhile: nothing waits on this. PR #1867 (lane other-checkout-cp-own) carries on.

options.gain: The record matches main and #1867. A copy still never overwrites a frozen file.
options.how: The record says: "A `cp` from a frozen source is a read; a frozen target is refused." The guard does not change.
options.label: Rewrite the sentence to match main

options.how: A lane changes the guard to refuse any cp whose source is frozen, and drops the test that allows it.
options.label: Keep the sentence; the guard refuses such a copy again
options.lose: A refusal on reads that do no harm: a false alarm you learn to skip.
